title: Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation for Multiple Tunnel Defects Under Complex Environments
abstract: arXiv:2611.19981v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Automated tunnel-lining inspection must segment different defect geometries: cracks are thin, elongated, and connectivity-sensitive, whereas leakage, lining falling off, and segment damage are spatially extensive and context-dependent. Existing approaches generally apply a common decoder across defect classes or introduce boundary, topology, and directional mechanisms as isolated enhancements. This paper introduces Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation (MDS), in which defect morphology becomes the organising principle for feature routing, decoding, and interaction. A supervised routing module partitions multiscale encoder features into complementary linear and areal streams. translated_title: 复杂环境下多种隧道缺陷的形态解耦分割
translated_abstract: 自动化隧道衬砌检测需要分割不同几何形态的缺陷：裂缝细长且对连通性敏感，而渗漏、衬砌脱落和管片破损则在空间上范围较大且高度依赖上下文。现有方法通常对所有缺陷类别使用统一的解码器，或将边界、拓扑和方向机制作为孤立的增强手段引入。本文提出了形态解耦分割（Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation, MDS），将缺陷形态作为特征路由、解码与交互的组织原则。一个有监督路由模块将多尺度编码器特征划分为互补的线状流和面状流。线状流采用带图像条件方向假设的可变形条带注意力，在不预设固定水平或垂直方向的前提下保持裂缝的连续性；面状流则将金字塔池化与特征金字塔融合相结合，以捕捉……（原文此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出形态解耦分割框架（MDS），以缺陷形态（线状/面状）为核心组织特征路由、解码与交互，从而在复杂隧道环境中同时精准分割细长裂缝与渗漏、衬砌脱落等大面积缺陷。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation (MDS), which organizes feature routing, decoding, and interaction around defect morphology, enabling accurate segmentation of both thin elongated cracks and extensive areal defects in complex tunnel environments.
